title: US Stocks Surge Near Week’s End, Capping Record-Breaking Gains – AP News
body:
U.S. equities closed Friday on a modest rally, nudging the S&P 500 up 0.6 percent and erasing most of the losses it had suffered over the previous two sessions. The gain capped a historic week in which the benchmark index not only shattered its own record highs but also posted the longest stretch of consecutive daily advances in more than three decades. While the American market pressed forward, investors elsewhere remained on the fence, leaving global markets in a mixed‑state of indecision.

The S&P 500’s resurgence was driven largely by a rebound in technology and consumer‑discretionary stocks, which had been hit hardest by earlier concerns over tightening monetary policy and lingering supply‑chain disruptions. Apple, Microsoft and Amazon each added roughly 1½ percent to their respective sector averages, buoyed by better‑than‑expected earnings guidance and renewed optimism about demand for cloud services and premium devices. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.2 percent, weighed down by a modest decline in industrials such as Caterpillar and United Technologies, whose shares fell on worries that higher interest rates could dampen capital‑intensive projects.

Analysts attribute the week’s extraordinary performance to a confluence of factors. First, the Federal Reserve’s recent decision to keep rates steady, coupled with signals that any future hikes would be data‑dependent, eased the anxiety that had been building since the central bank’s aggressive tightening cycle began in 2022. Second, corporate earnings season has entered its peak, and a growing number of companies have reported results that beat consensus estimates, reinforcing confidence that the economy remains resilient despite slower growth forecasts. Finally, the dollar’s modest retreat against a basket of major currencies has helped lift the earnings outlook for multinational firms, whose overseas revenues now translate into higher dollar‑denominated profits.

Outside the United States, market sentiment was far less uniform. In Europe, the Stoxx 600 hovered near flat, with defensive sectors such as utilities and health care providing a modest cushion while banking stocks lagged amid lingering concerns about credit quality in the Eurozone. Asian markets painted a similarly muted picture: Japan’s Nikkei slipped 0.3 percent, pressured by a weaker yen and tepid consumer sentiment, while China’s Shanghai Composite struggled to break out of a narrow trading range as investors awaited clearer signals from Beijing on stimulus measures. The divergent trajectories underscore the growing importance of domestic policy cues and regional economic data in shaping investor behavior.

The rally also highlighted the increasing influence of passive investment vehicles. Exchange‑traded funds (ETFs) that track the S&P 500 accounted for a substantial portion of the week’s net inflows, with investors favoring low‑cost, diversified exposure over individual stock picks. This trend has amplified the market’s responsiveness to macro‑level news, such as central bank announcements, while diminishing the impact of isolated corporate events. Nonetheless, active managers still found opportunities, particularly in small‑cap and emerging‑market segments where earnings surprises continue to drive price action.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching several key variables that could determine whether the momentum sustains or stalls. The Federal Reserve’s next policy meeting, slated for early next month, will likely focus on the trajectory of inflation and labor market tightness, both of which remain above the central bank’s long‑term targets. In addition, upcoming economic releases—including U.S. consumer confidence, durable goods orders, and the first‑quarter GDP estimate—will provide further insight into the health of the underlying economy. Finally, geopolitical developments, especially the evolving situation in Ukraine and trade negotiations between the United States and China, could inject fresh volatility into risk‑on assets.

If the Fed signals a pause in rate hikes and corporate earnings continue to outpace expectations, the S&P 500 may well extend its record‑setting run into the next trading week. Conversely, any surprise uptick in inflation or a sharp correction in high‑valuation tech stocks could prompt a swift reversal. For now, investors appear cautiously optimistic, buoyed by the week’s gains but aware that the market’s next move hinges on a delicate balance of monetary policy, economic data and global risk factors.
